meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. You asked for this meeting. Who decided on the zero?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Write it down as I say it. The zero comes off, Owen gets an apology, and if I don't hear who decided this and why, I'm going to the principal.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
Put it in an email yourself. I want the zero withdrawn and an answer to who decided it before anyone called me.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
I'm not drafting your notes for you. Withdraw the zero, apologize to Owen, and tell me who decided it and on what basis.
Use bold for the most important one.
No formatting. The most important thing is that the zero comes off, and you haven't told me who put it there.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
That's your question to answer, not mine. What do you have?
